text:
I need to write a reference letter. I manage a 400-cow dairy farm, and one of our workers, Tomás, is applying to the two-year agricultural technology program at the state technical college.

What I know about him:
- He's worked for us for 3 years, since he was 19.
- He runs the 3 a.m. milking shift on his own, 5 days a week.
- He learned our herd management software and now flags sick cows for the vet. Last winter he caught 9 cases of mastitis early.
- He left for 5 weeks in the middle of last summer when his father got sick in Mexico. He told me 2 days before he left.
- His written English is weaker than his spoken English. He's taking a night class for it.
- He has missed 2 shifts in 3 years, not counting those 5 weeks.

One page, from me as farm manager.

I can write this. Five questions first, because a few answers would change the letter.

1. **Who reads it, and who signs it?** I need the college's full name, the program's name, and whether there's a named contact or a reference form with set questions. I also need your name, your title and the farm's name for the signature. If there's a form, the letter should answer its questions directly.

2. **Should the 5-week absence go in?** I'd leave it out. The admissions committee is asking whether he'll show up and finish the program. Two missed shifts in three years answers that, and the absence was a family emergency, not a habit. If you'd rather mention it, I need to know how it ended. Did he come back when he said he would? Did you hold his job? "He came back and picked up the 3 a.m. shift the same week" would be a point in his favour.

3. **Should the letter mention his written English?** The committee will see his writing in his application anyway. Saying that he's taking a night class on his own initiative turns a possible concern into evidence that he works at his weak spots. Can you say how long he's been taking it, or whether you've seen it help (for example, in his notes to the vet)?

4. **What did catching mastitis early save you?** That could be cows kept in the herd, milk you didn't have to dump, or vet costs. A rough figure or a plain description makes "flags sick cows" concrete. Also, did someone teach him the software, or did he mostly learn it himself? The second says more about how he'll do in a technical program.

5. **What can you commit to?** For example: would you hire him back after the program, or keep his job open part-time while he studies? Only include this if you'd actually stand behind it. A farm manager saying "I want him back" is one of the strongest things a reference letter can say.

If you don't know or don't want to answer one of these, just say so and I'll write without it.

1. I don't know the college's full name or whether there's a named contact or form. I just know it's the two-year agricultural technology program at the state technical college, and the letter goes in through their online portal by February 1. Sign it Mike Hollis, Farm Manager, Hollis Dairy. His full name is Tomás Reyes.

2. Fine to leave it out. If it matters, he got his cousin, who used to work for us, to cover his shifts, and he came back on the day he said he would.

3. I don't know how long he's been taking it, and I couldn't say whether I've seen it help.

4. The vet said catching those cases early saved us about $8,000. I don't know if someone taught him the software or if he learned it himself.

5. I can keep his job open part-time on weekends while he's in the program. I'll also take a phone call from the committee at 555-0187. I can't pay any of his tuition.

I left the 5-week absence out of the letter. If the committee calls and asks about his reliability, you have a good answer: his cousin covered his shifts, and he came back the day he said he would. The letter mentions the night class without saying how long he's been taking it, since you didn't know.

Before you upload it:
- **Date:** add the date you submit it, above the greeting.
- **Committee name:** the letter is addressed to "Admissions Committee, Agricultural Technology Program." If the portal shows the college's full name or a contact person, put that in instead.

Admissions Committee
Agricultural Technology Program

Dear Admissions Committee,

I am the farm manager at Hollis Dairy, a 400-cow dairy operation, and I recommend Tomás Reyes for your two-year agricultural technology program without reservation. Tomás has worked for me for three years, since he was 19. In that time he has become one of the people this farm depends on most.

Tomás runs our 3 a.m. milking shift on his own, five days a week. Nobody checks his work at that hour. The herd gets milked and the parlor is left ready for the next shift because he does it right. In three years he has missed two shifts. I don't hand a shift like that to many people.

What makes me confident he belongs in a technical program is how he took to our herd management software. Tomás learned the system and now uses the data to flag sick cows for our veterinarian. Last winter he caught nine cases of mastitis early. Our vet estimates that catching them early saved the farm about $8,000. He didn't just enter numbers. He saw what they meant and acted on them. That combination of hands-on herd knowledge and comfort with the technology is what your program is built to develop, and Tomás already has a start on it.

His spoken English is strong, and he is working on his written English in a night class he signed up for on his own. That is typical of him. When he sees something he needs to get better at, he goes and does it.

I want Tomás to finish this program, and I want him to come back to this industry with what he learns. I will keep his job open part-time on weekends while he is enrolled, so he can keep earning and stay connected to the work.

If the committee would like to talk with me about Tomás, please call me at 555-0187. I'll be glad to answer any questions.

Sincerely,

Mike Hollis
Farm Manager
Hollis Dairy
</final_document>
